hey there -

1.4.20 is out and I haven't read too closely but this looks pretty much the same as #6678 which is fixed.  please confirm on your end, thanks!
I have the exact same issue with 1.4.20, so the problem is elsewhere...

OK before I get into this, your example uses private API:

    print(x.union(y)._from_self(sa.sql.func.count(sa.sql.literal_column("*"))).enable_eagerloads(False))

if the undesirable behavior involves using a private method like that, this is not supported.

can you provide a simple, single query using only supported APIs and illustrate a SQL round trip using SQLite which fails to return the correct results?  thanks.

I'm not really using the private API, I couldn't find out to print the count query itself, so i looked at query.count() implementation, and just used that to print out the query

This is what i really wanted to show:
```
print(x.union(y))
print(x.union(y).count())
```

Maybe i could have used echo=True on the engine, and just pasting the log output to get the actual query, but the end result is the same. The queries are not generated properly since 1.4.19

Adapted script to use actual sqlite roundtrip and remove use of private API

```python
import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship, sessionmaker

e = sa.create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)

DeclarativeBase = declarative_base()


class Parent(DeclarativeBase):
    __tablename__ = "parent"
    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)


class EventInvitation(DeclarativeBase):
    __tablename__ = "a"

    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, sa.ForeignKey("parent.id"))
    parent = relationship(Parent)


class EventResponse(DeclarativeBase):
    __tablename__ = "b"

    id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, primary_key=True)
    parent_id = sa.Column(sa.Integer, sa.ForeignKey("parent.id"))
    parent = relationship(Parent)


DeclarativeBase.metadata.create_all(e)

Session = sessionmaker(bind=e)
session = Session()

parent_id = 1
x = (
    session.query(EventInvitation)
    .filter(EventInvitation.parent_id == parent_id)
    .outerjoin(EventResponse, (EventResponse.parent_id == EventInvitation.parent_id))
    .with_entities(EventInvitation, EventResponse)
)
y = (
    session.query(EventResponse)
    .filter(EventResponse.parent_id == parent_id)
    .outerjoin(EventInvitation, (EventInvitation.parent_id == EventResponse.parent_id))
    .with_entities(EventInvitation, EventResponse)
)
x.union(y).all()
x.union(y).count()

```

OK, can you confirm the _from_self() and count() aren't necessary here, the query is different just printing (x.union(y)), the LEFT OUTER JOIN is added on the outside regardless.      the with_entities() use here is getting tripped up in either case.    sorry the use of "unions" and the "enable_eagerloads()" put me right into the mindset of the #6678 family of issues but i see this is just the new with_entities targeting getting a little confused.    with_entities has not been working at all throughout 1.4 so it's also surprising that you had a case that *was* working.

Yes, I put the count()/_from_self there just to show that it was somehow accumulating the left outer join several times across the subqueries, but the basic problem is already present just with the x.union(y), sorry if that was unclear.

We use with_entities quite a lot, to fetch only part of the query (sometimes just columns, sometimes just some entity instead of all, sometimes to get two joined entities from a query, like here). 1.4 was a bit rough in that respect, I had to sprinkle some select_from() calls here and there to get it mostly working, that was until the fix landed in 1.4.19. In this particular case, no select_from() was needed, but it triggered something wrong, apparently.

Just to clarify: our real use-case is to have q = x.union(y); return q[:5], q.count() somewhere inside a paginating API, so both should work, but i'm guessing that fixing the x.union(y) will make q.count() work as well

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**clear new Query._memoized_select_entities in _from_selectable** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/2945
